Courts across the country issued injunctions blocking major provisions; in April 2025, a DC district court found the president's authority was at its lowest ebb because the order contradicted the manifest will of Congress; in June 2025, a Boston court blocked five additional provisions on behalf of 19 states. A Congressional Research Service analysis published September 16, 2025, concluded the order purports to change the rules of federal elections in ways the president lacked constitutional authority to do. The Brennan Center's August 2025 report documented how the EO was being combined with DOJ task forces, DOGE database access, and personnel purges to construct a comprehensive federal apparatus for controlling election outcomes.

title: Trump Pressure Triggers Wave of State Voter Suppression Laws Ahead of 2026 Midterms
synopsis: Following Trump's EO 14248 and his relentless promotion of noncitizen-voter fraud myths, at least 13 states advanced legislation aligned with his election demands out of at least one chamber between January 2025 and mid-2026, according to a Votebeat analysis. Florida, Mississippi, Utah, South Dakota, and Wyoming passed laws requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register — documents that half of U.S. citizens do not possess. Florida's law additionally barred students from using student IDs at polls and stripped accepted forms of ID to align with the federal SAVE America Act. At least 67 million voter registrations — primarily from Republican-controlled states — were run through a DHS citizenship verification database by May 2026, flagging tens of thousands; in some states, voters had as little as 30 days to prove their eligibility before suspension. Five Republican-controlled states eliminated grace periods for late-arriving mail ballots after Trump's EO called for it. Florida state Rep. Jenna Persons-Mulicka said her proof-of-citizenship bill fully answers the president's call; Wyoming Secretary of State Chuck Gray said his state's measure was key in supporting President Trump's pivotal work. Voting rights advocates identified married women, transgender people, elderly Black voters, and Puerto Ricans with pre-2010 birth certificates as communities disproportionately harmed by the new requirements.

title: Trump Retaliates Against Brad Raffensperger and Election Officials Who Refused to Overturn 2020
synopsis: Throughout 2025 and 2026, Trump and his DOJ constructed an apparatus of retaliation against officials who had certified the 2020 election. In a March 14, 2025 speech, Trump stated: What a difference a rigged and crooked election had on our country. And the people who did this to us should go to jail. An executive order directed DOJ to review the actions of Chris Krebs — Trump's own CISA director — because he denied that the 2020 election was rigged and stolen. The Georgia GOP's June 2025 convention passed a resolution calling for the party to block Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger from qualifying on the Republican ticket for daring to certify Biden's 2020 win. Trump endorsed Raffensperger's opponent Burt Jones — one of the fake electors — for governor. On May 13, 2026, Raffensperger's gubernatorial campaign reported an active threat and a bomb scare at a campaign event; Raffensperger said: When you stand on principle, some people will hate you, even want to try and hurt you. The Brennan Center documented that the administration's threats of prosecution were designed to ensure that election officials facing future pressure would capitulate rather than risk the retaliation Raffensperger endured for doing his job.

title: AI Deepfakes and Pro-Trump Bot Networks Flood 2026 Midterm Campaigns Without Federal Regulation
synopsis: By early 2026, at least 15 campaign ads featuring AI-generated content had run in federal, state, and local races, with no federal law requiring disclosure or prohibition — the Trump administration made no effort to regulate the technology and Congress had failed to pass pending bills. The National Republican Senatorial Committee released an AI-generated video in March 2026 depicting Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico reading real tweets, with the fabricated video presented as if authentic. A Trump-aligned outside group, Citizens for Sanity, produced a deepfake of Talarico in a dress singing; AI attack ads ran in Kentucky, Georgia, Massachusetts, and Texas primaries. A Reuters investigation published March 28, 2026, found AI deepfakes were expected to spread with few guardrails and that Republicans are embracing AI to a greater extent than Democrats. The New York Times discovered hundreds of fake pro-Trump AI-generated influencer accounts on Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook in April 2026, part of what experts described as a pre-midterm push using avatars created in bulk at low cost by content farms. The complete absence of federal enforcement — with the FEC lacking a quorum and the DOJ focused on targeting perceived enemies — left voters with no protection against a tidal wave of AI-generated political disinformation in the most consequential election of Trump's second term.

title: Trump Attempts Unconstitutional Pardon of Convicted Election Saboteur Tina Peters
synopsis: On December 12, 2025, Trump announced on Truth Social that he was granting a full Pardon to Tina Peters, the former Mesa County, Colorado, clerk sentenced to nine years in state prison for orchestrating a scheme to allow unauthorized access to county voting machines in 2021 — a scheme driven by Trump's false fraud claims. Democrats have been relentless in their targeting of TINA PETERS, a Patriot who simply wanted to make sure that our Elections were Fair and Honest, Trump posted falsely; Peters had been prosecuted by a Republican district attorney in a Republican county. The presidential pardon power extends only to federal crimes, and Peters was convicted entirely of state felonies — a fact acknowledged by Colorado Governor Jared Polis, Colorado AG Phil Weiser, and Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold, who called it a lawless intrusion on states' rights. The DOJ had asked Colorado to transfer Peters to federal custody — a request the state refused. Trump had in May 2025 called Peters a political prisoner and warned he would take harsh measures if she was not released. The episode followed a pattern of using the pardon machinery to declare that any election official who sought to stop fraud committed by Trump loyalists was a legitimate target for full presidential protection and rehabilitation.

title: Trump Administration Threatens State AGs and Election Officials With Prosecution for Certifying 2020 Results
synopsis: The Trump DOJ under Attorney General Pam Bondi — who had herself spread election fraud claims — created multiple enforcement structures targeting officials involved in the 2020 election: the Weaponization Working Group, a New Jersey U.S. Attorney's Office Election Integrity Task Force, and a Washington DC Special Unit for Election Accountability. The Brennan Center documented that these bodies were directed to investigate perceived enemies, including the Manhattan DA, the New York AG, and anyone who prosecuted January 6 defendants. FBI Director Kash Patel stated publicly: We're going to come after the people in the media who lied about American citizens, who helped Joe Biden rig presidential elections. Trump himself told an audience in March 2025: The people who did this to us should go to jail. In the summer 2026 Minneapolis immigration dispute, AG Bondi sent a letter to Minnesota officials suggesting the state should hand over unredacted voter rolls to DOJ, which state officials interpreted as a coercive demand tied to potential withdrawal of ICE agents. The Brennan Center concluded that an election official fearful of criminal charges might succumb to pressure to aggressively purge voters or engage in outright election subversion, achieving through threat what Trump's 2020 pressure campaign on Raffensperger failed to accomplish through direct requests.

title: USPS Mail Consolidations and Trump EO Create Ballot Delivery Crisis Before 2026 Midterms
synopsis: A combination of Trump executive orders and Postal Service network consolidations produced a worsening mail ballot crisis heading into the 2026 midterms. Under the Delivering for America overhaul, USPS consolidated mail processing into roughly 60 regional hubs, meaning ballots in rural areas now traveled an average of 139 miles — and sometimes 500 miles — before being postmarked, causing a lag of one or more days between when a voter mailed a ballot and when it was stamped. A December 31, 2025, USPS rule change acknowledged that postmarks no longer necessarily reflect the date the agency first received mail. In California's June 2026 primary, more than 148,000 ballots — 63% of rejections — arrived too late despite the state's seven-day grace period; Wisconsin reported hundreds of late ballots in April 2026. Postmaster General David Steiner told a Senate committee in June 2026 the agency was out of cash. Trump's March 2026 EO 14399 then directed USPS to refuse to carry any mail ballot unless the voter appeared on a federal citizenship-verified list — effectively deputizing the bankrupt, operationally stressed postal service as a voter eligibility gatekeeper for the first time in American history. Election officials in Kansas and Michigan advised voters to abandon mail voting entirely and use drop boxes instead.

title: Trump Pressures Texas Redistricting to Flip 5 Democratic House Seats, Igniting National Map-Drawing Arms Race
synopsis: In July 2025, at Trump's direct urging, Texas Republicans undertook an extraordinary mid-decade redraw of the state's congressional districts, targeting five Democratic-held U.S. House seats with the explicit goal of protecting the GOP's fragile House majority ahead of the 2026 midterms — a move upending decades of precedent against mid-cycle partisan redistricting. Trump applied direct pressure to multiple other Republican-controlled legislatures; in Indiana, Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith confirmed that unnamed Trump administration officials threatened the state's federal funding if it refused to redistrict. The gambit ignited a national redistricting arms race, with Democratic governors — led by California's Gavin Newsom — threatening retaliatory redraws in blue states. Meanwhile, Trump's administration and the Republican-controlled Congress continued to block Puerto Rico statehood and Washington DC statehood, both of which would add likely Democratic senators and representatives; Puerto Rico's statehood referendum had been approved by voters in November 2024 but the 119th Congress refused to act. The Votebeat analysis found that Trump had become the most interventionist president in the history of state election administration, directly threatening officials by name and promising to support primary challengers against Republicans who resisted his redistricting demands.

title: Trump Withdraws From Paris Climate Agreement on Inauguration Day — Again
synopsis: Hours after being sworn in on January 20, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14162, titled Putting America First In International Environmental Agreements, directing the U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations to immediately submit formal written notification of withdrawal from the 2015 Paris Agreement. The order declared the withdrawal effective immediately upon this provision of notification, leaving the United States as one of only four countries outside the accord — alongside Iran, Libya, and Yemen. The move eliminated all U.S. financial commitments under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, including billions in pledged contributions to the Green Climate Fund. Trump had performed the same withdrawal in 2017, but Biden rejoined in January 2021; this second departure signaled permanent American abandonment of international climate cooperation. Scientists warned the exit would encourage other nations to weaken their own commitments, and U.S. allies condemned the action as a strategic and moral abdication at a moment when global temperatures had hit record highs three years running.

title: Trump Declares National Energy Emergency to Fast-Track Fossil Fuel Drilling
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14156, Declaring a National Energy Emergency, invoking the National Emergencies Act to grant federal agencies sweeping authority to bypass environmental review and fast-track oil, gas, coal, and mineral permitting on federal lands. At the signing, Trump declared, The inflation crisis was caused by massive overspending and escalating energy prices — we will drill, baby, drill, despite U.S. oil production already being at record highs. The order directed agency heads to identify and use all lawful emergency authorities to expedite domestic energy production, and called for emergency Clean Water Act permitting provisions to streamline Army Corps approvals for pipelines and infrastructure. It also authorized potential use of the Defense Production Act for energy projects and demanded an assessment of military fuel supply vulnerabilities. Environmental groups immediately filed legal challenges, arguing no genuine emergency existed and the order was a pretext to gut NEPA and Clean Water Act protections in service of the fossil fuel industry.

title: EPA Dismantled: 23% Workforce Cut, Research Office Eliminated, Enforcement Gutted
synopsis: On July 18, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the agency was eliminating its Office of Research and Development — the scientific backbone of EPA for over five decades, with roughly 1,500 scientists — and cutting the agency's total workforce by at least 23%, from 16,155 employees in January to 12,448, the smallest EPA headcount since the mid-1980s. The restructuring, Zeldin claimed, would save $748.8 million, but critics described it as the dismantling of the agency's scientific credibility. The first wave of cuts had begun February 14, 2025, when 388 probationary employees were terminated; by March 2025 additional layoffs were accelerating. Zeldin announced on March 12, 2025 what he called the greatest day of deregulation in U.S. history, proposing to roll back more than 30 environmental rules simultaneously, including reconsideration of the 2009 Endangerment Finding that underpins virtually all EPA climate regulation. Justin Chen, president of EPA's largest union, called the cuts devastating, citing the dismantling of research labs across the country. An independent report released in February 2026 found that EPA brought only 16 lawsuits against polluters in all of 2025, an 81% decline from Trump's own first term and a historic low.

title: Trump Opens National Monuments to Oil, Gas, and Mining — Millions of Protected Acres at Risk
synopsis: On February 3, 2025, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum issued an order directing a comprehensive review of national monuments created by previous presidents, immediately raising alarms about the fate of Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante in Utah — two monuments encompassing over 3.2 million acres that Trump had already shrunk in his first term. By April 24, 2025, The Washington Post reported that Interior officials were actively analyzing at least six monuments for boundary reductions to enable energy and mineral extraction, including Bears Ears (which contains uranium deposits), Grand Staircase-Escalante (which overlies coal reserves), Baaj Nwaavjo I'tah Kukveni-Ancestral Footprints of the Grand Canyon in Arizona, Ironwood Forest in Arizona, Organ Mountains-Desert Peaks in New Mexico, and Chuckwalla in California. The review was conducted in secret, with officials speaking to reporters only on condition of anonymity, and was predicated on the administration's declared national energy emergency — despite energy production already being at record levels. Indigenous tribes and conservation groups warned that reductions would permit mining and drilling in some of the most ecologically and culturally significant landscapes in the American West, with impacts to the Colorado Plateau watershed and irreplaceable archaeological sites.

title: Trump Kills Biden EV Mandates and Guts CAFE Fuel Economy Standards
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order revoking Biden's 2021 goal of 50% EV sales by 2030 and freezing $5 billion in unspent EV charging infrastructure funds, while directing EPA to reconsider emissions rules that would have required 30-56% EV sales by 2032. Then on December 3, 2025, the Trump administration proposed slashing the Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards from Biden's 50.4 miles-per-gallon fleet average target for 2031 down to 34.5 mpg — a 32% rollback that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's own analysis said would increase fuel consumption by roughly 100 billion gallons through 2050, costing Americans up to $185 billion more in gas expenses over that period. The White House called the CAFE reset delivering a win for American families, claiming it would lower car sticker prices by about $930. In June 2025, Trump signed a joint resolution ending California's authority to set its own stricter EV standards — effectively nullifying similar rules in 17 other states — and in July 2025 Congress zeroed out civil penalties for automakers that violate CAFE rules. Environmental and public health advocates warned the combined rollbacks would dramatically increase greenhouse gas emissions, deepen U.S. oil dependence, and set the domestic auto industry back by a decade compared to European and Chinese competitors.

title: Offshore Drilling Expansion: Atlantic, Pacific, and Arctic Opened to Oil Leases
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order revoking Biden's 2024 ban on drilling in approximately 625 million acres of U.S. coastal waters and repealing a 2023 memo that had barred oil drilling across 16 million Arctic acres. By April 18, 2025, the Interior Department began public input for a new five-year offshore leasing program explicitly targeting the Arctic and new regions. On November 20, 2025, Interior Secretary Burgum issued a Secretary's Order launching the 11th National Outer Continental Shelf Oil and Gas Leasing Program, proposing up to 34 lease sales across 1.27 billion acres — including 21 planning areas off Alaska, six off the Pacific coast, and areas in the Gulf of America — replacing what officials called the smallest offshore leasing plan ever published. Separately, on January 20, Trump signed EO 14153 directing expedited leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge's Coastal Plain, reversing Biden's 2021 halt of the ANWR program. Environmental groups warned that opening the Pacific and Atlantic coasts — where no offshore infrastructure exists and where states have consistently opposed drilling — represented a reckless bet on fossil fuels that would threaten fishing industries, coastal tourism, and marine ecosystems for decades to come.

title: Clean Power Plan 2.0 Gutted — EPA Proposes Eliminating All GHG Standards for Power Plants
synopsis: On June 11, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, flanked by Republican lawmakers at EPA headquarters, proposed repealing all greenhouse gas emissions standards for the U.S. power sector under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act — effectively eliminating both the 2015 Obama-era standards for new fossil fuel plants and Biden's 2024 Clean Power Plan 2.0 emission guidelines for existing coal, oil, and gas plants. The proposal also moved to repeal 2024 amendments to the Mercury and Air Toxics Standards that had been requiring coal plants to reduce brain-damaging mercury emissions. Zeldin claimed the rollbacks would save $120 million per year for electric utilities. Environmental groups countered that the repeals would increase cancer-causing and neurotoxic air pollution, lock in decades of carbon emissions, and kill thousands of Americans prematurely each year from worsened air quality. EPA had telegraphed the move on March 12, 2025, when Zeldin announced it as part of what he called the most consequential day of deregulation in U.S. history. A public hearing on the GHG repeal was held July 8, 2025, with EPA planning to finalize the rule by spring 2026.

title: Trump Kills Methane Fee — Oil and Gas Industry's $900-Per-Ton Pollution Charge Erased
synopsis: On March 14, 2025, President Trump signed H.J.Res. 35 — a Congressional Review Act joint resolution — into law as Public Law 119-2, nullifying EPA's Waste Emissions Charge rule that had imposed a $900-per-ton fee on oil and gas producers releasing excess methane, a fee that would have escalated to $1,500 per ton by 2026. The WEC had been a centerpiece of the Inflation Reduction Act's climate provisions, representing the first-ever federal price on methane pollution, which traps 80 times more heat per molecule than CO2 over a 20-year period. The House had passed the resolution February 26, 2025, and the Senate followed party-line 52-47 on February 27, with the repeal introduced by Rep. August Pfluger (R-TX). On May 12, 2025, EPA formally removed the WEC regulations from the Code of Federal Regulations. Scientists estimated the methane fee, had it remained in force, would have incentivized dramatic reductions in leaks from the roughly 900,000 U.S. oil and gas wells — methane being responsible for roughly 30% of current global warming. The repeal was celebrated by major oil and gas trade groups and came the same week the administration was proposing separate rollbacks on power plant emissions and vehicle standards.

title: NOAA Gutted: 800+ Weather Scientists Fired, Climate Research Programs Dismantled
synopsis: On February 27-28, 2025, the Trump administration fired more than 800 probationary employees from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration — approximately 6-10% of its 12,000-13,000-person workforce — in a single wave of terminations that devastated the National Weather Service, the agency's climate modeling divisions, and its satellite operations. Among those fired were meteorologists performing daily local forecasts, scientists at the Geophysical Fluid Dynamics Laboratory in Princeton who maintain global climate models, and staff at the Environmental Modeling Center responsible for keeping weather prediction computers operational. The NOAA Great Lakes Environmental Research Laboratory immediately suspended all public communications due to staffing shortages, and weather balloon launches in Kotzebue, Alaska — critical for upper-air data used in forecasting across the continent — were suspended the same day. By March 11, 2025, the AP reported a second round of more than 1,000 additional layoffs was underway. UCLA climate scientist Daniel Swain called the firings profoundly alarming, noting cuts to mission-critical and life-saving roles at the National Weather Service. Tom Di Liberto, a meteorologist fired from NOAA Communications, warned: We will be less prepared for the next disaster and the disaster after that.

title: EPA Enforcement Collapses to Historic Low — Polluters Given Effective Immunity
synopsis: A comprehensive report by the Environmental Integrity Project, released in February 2026, documented that the Trump EPA brought only 16 civil lawsuits against polluters on behalf of the Department of Justice in all of 2025 — a figure 81% lower than the first year of Trump's own first term in 2017 (86 cases), 76% lower than Biden's first year (67 cases), and 87% lower than Obama's second-term first year. Superfund consent decrees hit a new low with just 7 in 2025 versus 31 in 2017; Clean Air Act consent decrees numbered only 1 versus 26 in 2017; and Clean Water Act consent decrees dropped to 4, a record low. EPA administrative monetary penalties against polluters totaled only $41 million through September 2025, down $8 million in real terms from Biden's first year. At least a third of DOJ's environmental enforcement attorneys left the department during 2025, gutting the pipeline of cases. In a December 5, 2025 internal memo, EPA's Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance outlined a new obstacle course requiring political clearance for enforcement actions, and reframed the agency's mission away from overzealous enforcement intended to cripple industry based on climate zealotry. EIP Executive Director Jen Duggan declared: Our nation's landmark environmental laws are meaningless when EPA does not enforce the rules.

title: Willow Expansion: Trump Opens 82% of Alaska's Petroleum Reserve to Drilling
synopsis: Trump's administration moved on multiple fronts to massively expand oil drilling in Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve, the largest tract of public land in the United States at 23.5 million acres. On December 5, 2025, Trump signed Senate Joint Resolution 80, using the Congressional Review Act to revoke Biden-era 2022 restrictions that had protected ecologically sensitive areas of the NPR-A from drilling. On December 22, 2025, the Bureau of Land Management approved a new management plan opening approximately 82% of the NPR-A to oil and gas leasing — reverting to Trump's 2020 plan and announcing the first lease sale in the reserve since 2019. Separately, in November 2025 the administration fast-tracked ConocoPhillips' winter exploration program near its giant Willow discovery, approving plans for 4 exploratory wells, 60 miles of ice roads, seismic testing across 300 square miles, and the extraction of 90 million gallons of freshwater from Arctic lakes — all with only a one-week public comment period, the first day of which fell on Veterans Day. An Alaska Native group, Sovereign Inu_piat for a Living Arctic, sued to stop the exploration, citing inadequate environmental review and threats to the Teshekpuk caribou herd. Environmental groups warned that Willow's approval as a foot in the door for broader Arctic industrialization had been confirmed.

title: National Forests and BLM Lands Opened to Logging and Mining — 280 Million Acres Targeted
synopsis: On March 1, 2025, Trump signed an executive order titled Immediate Expansion of American Timber Production, directing the Forest Service and BLM to ramp up logging across 280 million acres of federal lands by bypassing Endangered Species Act consultations, creating categorical exclusions from environmental review under NEPA, and setting multi-year timber sale volume targets. The order came weeks after the administration fired 3,400 U.S. Forest Service employees — about 10% of the agency's workforce — on February 13-15, 2025, eliminating trail maintenance crews, fuel-reduction specialists, and wildfire support staff. On April 4, 2025, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins issued an emergency designation covering more than half of U.S. national forests that stripped outside groups, tribes, and local governments of their right to object to logging proposals before they were finalized. Separately, a March 20, 2025 executive order on domestic mineral production directed Interior Secretary Burgum to prioritize mining as the primary land use on mineral-rich federal lands, including areas near national parks and Indigenous sacred sites. The Center for Biological Diversity warned that the mining order put more than 120,000 active mining claims within 30 miles of national parks on a fast track toward approval.

title: Trump Bans Offshore Wind — Total Moratorium Issued on His First Day Back in Office
synopsis: On January 20, 2025, Trump signed a presidential memorandum withdrawing all areas of the Outer Continental Shelf from disposition for wind energy leasing indefinitely, effective January 21, halting new offshore wind leases across the entire Atlantic, Pacific, and Gulf coasts, and suspending all federal approvals, permits, rights-of-way, and loans for both offshore and onshore wind projects pending an administration review. The order also targeted a specific Idaho project — the 231-turbine Lava Ridge Wind Project — ordering a moratorium on all activities under its federal permit. Trump justified the anti-wind order by falsely claiming offshore wind turbines caused increases in whale deaths, saying they kill your birds and they ruin your beautiful landscapes, despite no scientific evidence supporting these claims. The moratorium threatened to strand billions of dollars in offshore wind investments by companies including Orsted, Avangrid, and Dominion, and threatened to block the buildout of an energy sector the U.S. had been developing to compete with China and Europe. Analysts warned the indefinite halt would cost tens of thousands of clean energy jobs, raise long-term electricity costs, and cede American leadership in offshore wind technology to foreign competitors at a moment when the industry was nearing commercial viability at scale.

title: WOTUS Gutted — Trump Rule Would Strip Federal Protection From 80% of U.S. Wetlands
synopsis: On November 17, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Assistant Secretary of the Army Adam Telle announced a proposed rule redefining Waters of the United States under the Clean Water Act that would, according to EPA and Army Corps' own regulatory impact analysis, leave 81% of U.S. wetlands by acreage without federal protection — only about 17.4 million of the roughly 110 million mapped acres in the contiguous United States would retain Clean Water Act coverage. The proposal, posted to the Federal Register on November 20 with a 45-day comment period, built upon the 2023 Supreme Court Sackett v. EPA ruling but adopted an even more restrictive interpretation than Biden's post-Sackett conforming rule, adding requirements that wetlands must hold surface water during the wet season to qualify. In Arizona, just 2.4% of wetlands would be covered; in Iowa, only 5%. Zeldin framed the rule as putting a dagger through the heart of climate change religion, while farm bureaus and real estate developers praised it as ending federal overreach. Environmentalists called it a giveaway to developers, ranchers, and industry that would accelerate the loss of wetlands that filter drinking water, provide flood mitigation, and sustain endangered wildlife — at a moment when the U.S. has already lost more than half its original wetland acreage since European settlement.

title: Trump Guts Wildfire Prevention Funding Weeks After Los Angeles Burns
synopsis: In the weeks immediately following the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires — expected to be the costliest in U.S. history with losses potentially reaching $35 billion — the Trump administration froze wildfire prevention funding, fired thousands of firefighting-adjacent personnel, and halted seasonal firefighter hiring across the country. By February 13-14, 2025, reports confirmed that the administration had frozen all remaining funds from the $3 billion in wildfire mitigation money appropriated through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act, canceling contracts with non-profits like the Oregon-based Lomakatsi Restoration Project. On February 15, 2025, the New York Times reported that 3,400 U.S. Forest Service employees — roughly 10% of the agency's workforce — had been terminated, eliminating trail crews, fuel-reduction specialists, and training instructors who form the backbone of wildfire preparedness. A planned 151,434-acre prescribed burn in Everglades National Park was canceled; training programs for forest firefighters were scrapped mid-season; and seasonal hiring stalled just as fire season approached. Federal firefighters told ProPublica that it's always cheaper to do a prescribed burn than to fight an escaped wildfire, while the annual area burned by U.S. wildfires over the past decade was already 43% larger than the historical average tracked since 1983.

title: Schedule F: Trump Purges 50,000 Deep State Civil Servants as Political Enemies
synopsis: On his first day in office, January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order reinstating and renaming Schedule F — a policy that strips civil service job protections from approximately 50,000 federal employees, reclassifying them as at-will workers who can be fired without cause. The order was engineered by Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and OMB Director Russ Vought, both of whom had long championed the strategy during Trump's first term. Trump and his allies framed the entire career federal workforce as a conspiratorial deep state populated by enemies within who had sabotaged his first administration — rhetoric rejected by legal experts and historians as fabricated justification for a power grab unprecedented in modern presidencies. In parallel, Elon Musk's DOGE team conducted mass layoffs across dozens of agencies, with senior DOJ officials, Coast Guard commandants, and State Department diplomats dismissed within hours of the inauguration. The American Federation of Government Employees and AFSCME filed lawsuits in February 2025 alleging unconstitutional authority, with AFSCME President Lee Saunders stating Schedule F is a shameless attempt to politicize the federal workforce by replacing thousands of dedicated, qualified civil servants with political cronies. Critics noted the irony that Trump branded career civil servants enemies based purely on the conspiracy theory that loyalty to law rather than loyalty to Trump constitutes treason.

title: Trump Guts Pandemic Office and Silences CDC as Bird Flu Spreads Nationwide
synopsis: Within hours of taking office on January 20, 2025, the Trump administration ordered an immediate pause on all CDC communications — halting publication of the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, which had been published without interruption since 1952 — just as the H5N1 bird flu outbreak was actively spreading across dairy herds and farmworkers in multiple states. The White House Office of Pandemic Preparedness and Response Policy, a congressionally mandated office with a staff of 20 that had been coordinating the entire federal bird flu response, was gutted to a single remaining staffer by March 2025. By February 14, Reuters reported that CDC had withheld bird flu surveillance reports and canceled all congressional briefings and meetings with state health officials, with 11 sources describing confusion and concern as the federal response infrastructure collapsed. In April 2025, the administration conducted mass layoffs of 10,000 health agency workers across FDA, CDC, and NIH, firing staff working on measles, port health screening, and emergency disease response — former CDC Director Tom Frieden compared the communications blackout to telling your local fire department not to sound any fire alarms. Trump also canceled a $766 million Moderna H5N1 vaccine development contract in June 2025, even as HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. — a vaccine skeptic with a documented history of promoting lab-leak and government-cover-up conspiracy theories — was simultaneously dismantling the independent advisory committees that had governed vaccine policy for decades.

title: MAGA's Chemtrail Hysteria Becomes Law: Trump Allies Turn Cloud-Seeding Into a Federal Crisis
synopsis: A fringe conspiracy theory holding that the government secretly sprays harmful chemicals from aircraft to control weather or reduce population — known as chemtrails — surged into mainstream Republican politics in 2025, fueled directly by Trump's MAGA allies and amplified by the White House ecosystem. Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene declared Yes they can control the weather following Hurricane Helene in October 2024, and in July 2025 she introduced the Clear Skies Act to ban all weather modification and geoengineering. Former Trump National Security Adviser Michael Flynn spread unfounded claims blaming cloud-seeding company Rainmaker Technology for the July 4, 2025 Texas floods that killed more than 120 people, causing the small company's CEO Augustus Doricko to face nonstop pandemonium and doxxing threats. Republican governors in Florida and Tennessee signed legislation making weather modification a felony punishable by up to $100,000 in fines, and more than 20 states introduced similar bills, with Florida's Attorney General James Uthmeier suggesting in a public letter that weather modification may have triggered the Texas flooding. The EPA under Trump Administrator Lee Zeldin took the extraordinary step in July 2025 of creating new websites to debunk the chemtrails theory — an acknowledgment of how deeply the conspiracy had penetrated the Republican base — while militia leaders in Oklahoma publicly celebrated the physical attack on a weather radar tower, insisting meteorological equipment could manipulate the weather.

title: RFK Jr.'s HHS Unleashes Anti-Vaccine Conspiracy Orthodoxy, Triggers Worst Measles Crisis in 33 Years
synopsis: In 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. — who had spent decades falsely linking vaccines to autism and claiming government cover-up of vaccine injury data — was given full authority over the nation's public health apparatus, with catastrophic results. On June 9, 2025, Kennedy fired all 17 members of the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the independent scientific body that had shaped vaccine recommendations for decades, calling for a clean sweep and pledging to replace members with his own loyalists; he had already changed COVID-19 vaccine recommendations without consulting the committee. Kennedy's HHS canceled a $766 million Moderna H5N1 vaccine contract, required federally funded schools and clinics to accept religious and conscience-based exemptions to vaccine mandates, and shelved government promotional campaigns for flu shots in favor of messaging about informed consent. By July 31, 2025, CDC data showed kindergarten MMR vaccination rates fell to 92.5% — below the 95% herd immunity threshold — with vaccine exemptions reaching an all-time high of 3.6%; Idaho reached 15.4% exemption rates. Measles cases hit 1,333 confirmed cases in 2025, the highest count since the disease was declared eliminated in 2000, with a child dying of measles in rural West Texas in February 2025 — the first U.S. measles death in a decade. NBC News found that 77% of U.S. counties had experienced notable vaccination rate declines since 2019, with 67% of counties now below herd immunity levels for measles.

title: Trump Blames Newsom for Sabotaging California Wildfires With Fake Water Restoration Declaration
synopsis: As catastrophic wildfires devastated the Los Angeles area beginning January 7, 2025 — killing at least 10 people, forcing 180,000 evacuations, and destroying more than 10,000 structures — President-elect Donald Trump immediately launched a disinformation campaign blaming California Governor Gavin Newsom for deliberately causing the disaster. On January 8, 2025, Trump posted to Truth Social that Newsom refused to sign the water restoration declaration put before him that would have allowed millions of gallons of water to flow daily into many parts of California — a document that state officials confirmed does not exist, with Newsom's office calling it pure fiction. Trump claimed hydrants ran dry because Newsom diverted water to protect an essentially worthless fish called a smelt — a claim water policy experts called physically impossible, since Los Angeles receives its water primarily from the Colorado River and Owens Valley, not the Sacramento Delta; Peter Gleick of the Pacific Institute called the framing nothing short of irresponsible. Trump also falsely claimed there was NO MONEY IN FEMA when Congress had appropriated $29 billion specifically for FEMA's Disaster Relief Fund just weeks earlier. The conspiracy narrative included additional false claims that a billionaire couple was hoarding water and that firefighters had used women's handbags rather than proper equipment; online posts falsely attributed the fires to arson by MAGA-affiliated groups, fabricating police searches for persons of interest.

title: Trump Pardons QAnon Shaman, Oath Keepers, Proud Boys — Cementing Ties to Extremist Movement
synopsis: On his first day back in office, January 20, 2025, Trump issued a sweeping pardon covering all 1,500-plus people charged in the January 6, 2021 Capitol insurrection — including convicted violent felons, seditious conspiracy leaders, and the QAnon Shaman himself. Jacob Chansley, the face of QAnon's presence at January 6 who wore face paint and a horned fur headdress as he occupied the Senate chamber, was among those pardoned; he responded on X: THANK YOU PRESIDENT TRUMP!!! NOW I AM GONNA BUY SOME GUNS. Oath Keepers founder Stewart Rhodes, convicted of seditious conspiracy and sentenced to 18 years, and former Proud Boys leader Enrique Tarrio, also convicted of seditious conspiracy, were both freed within hours of the pardons — with Elon Musk's ally Paul Ingrassia at the DC jail wearing a tuxedo from an inaugural ball, crediting Musk as the mastermind behind the first releases. The pardons and commutations covered 14 far-right extremists from the Oath Keepers and Proud Boys convicted of orchestrating plots to violently stop the transfer of presidential power. Trump called the 1,500 convicted insurrectionists the hostages — a QAnon-adjacent framing suggesting a conspiracy that had imprisoned patriots rather than a prosecutorial response to documented seditious violence. A subsequent NBC News review of Trump's Truth Social AI posts found at least four posts containing references to QAnon conspiracy theory symbology, and the president continued to describe January 6 as a hostage situation through 2026.

title: Trump Repeats 2020 Stolen Election Lie 107 Times in Six Months Ahead of 2026 Midterms
synopsis: A Reuters review published May 26, 2026 found that President Trump had repeated his false claim that the 2020 election was stolen from him at least 107 times in the six months preceding the midterm elections — averaging more than four times per week — including seven posts in a single Saturday in April 2026 while a fragile ceasefire with Iran was in place. Trump repeated the stolen election claims during at least six meetings with foreign heads of state, two visits by professional sports teams to the White House, Hanukkah and Christmas observances, and his speech to the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026, where he said people will soon be prosecuted for what they did. On January 29, 2026, the FBI executed a search warrant on the election headquarters of Fulton County, Georgia, seeking 2020 ballots — a move critics called Trump using federal law enforcement to retroactively validate his disproven fraud narrative. Trump delivered a primetime address on July 16, 2026 — more than five and a half years after the election — claiming China stole 220 million voter files and that members of the deep state suppressed the findings; fact-checkers noted the documents he released actually confirmed China considered but did not deploy significant interference. An April 2026 Reuters/Ipsos poll found 63% of Republicans still believed the 2020 election was stolen, while Trump's 2020 rhetoric had become a loyalty test for his judicial nominees who refused under oath to confirm Biden won.

title: Trump's Worst of the Worst Immigration Lie: ICE Arrests Harmless Immigrants While 94% of Murderers Go Free
synopsis: Throughout 2025, President Trump and his border enforcement apparatus repeatedly claimed to be conducting the most targeted deportation campaign in history, focused on the worst of the worst violent criminals. But government data told a completely different story: Reuters reported in June 2025 that ICE detentions of individuals with no criminal charges or convictions rose by 800% in Trump's first months, from approximately 860 in January to 7,800 by June. NBC News obtained ICE booking data showing that of the 13,099 undocumented immigrants ICE had previously identified as convicted of homicide, only 752 were arrested in Trump's first eight months — a 6% apprehension rate — while almost half of all ICE detainees had no criminal conviction or charge of any kind. Homan continued to repeat the claim that 600,000 criminal illegal aliens were walking the streets — a figure FactCheck.org found to be systematically misleading, including legal immigrants, people charged but not convicted, and individuals who entered the country over 40 years ago. Trump claimed in an April 2025 Time interview that crime rates under Biden went through the roof and were added to by illegal immigrants — directly contradicting FBI data showing violent crime dropped during Biden's presidency; criminologists cited multiple peer-reviewed studies showing immigrants commit crimes at lower rates than native-born citizens.

title: RFK Jr.'s Anti-Vaccine Crusade as HHS Secretary Drives America's Measles Rate to 33-Year High
synopsis: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who spent decades promoting the thoroughly debunked claim that vaccines cause autism and accusing the CDC of conspiring to hide vaccine injury data, was confirmed as HHS Secretary in February 2025 and immediately began dismantling America's vaccination infrastructure. Kennedy launched a study of the Vaccine Safety Datalink database to investigate vaccine-autism links — a connection disproven in dozens of prior studies using the same data — while his anti-vaccine allies publicly claimed on social media that the CDC had obliterated the database to thwart Kennedy's investigation, a conspiracy theory the CDC flatly denied. On June 9, 2025, Kennedy fired all 17 members of ACIP — the independent scientific committee advising the CDC on vaccines — stating a clean sweep is needed to re-establish public confidence, and began replacing them with anti-vaccine loyalists including researcher Mark Geier, whose CDC data access had been revoked twice for protocol violations. By July 31, 2025, CDC data showed kindergarten vaccination rates had fallen for all reported vaccines during the 2024-2025 school year, with the MMR rate dropping to 92.5% — below the 95% herd immunity threshold — and vaccine exemptions hitting an all-time high of 3.6%; Idaho reached 15.4%, and 36 states saw exemption rates rise. America recorded 1,333 measles cases by late July 2025 — the highest annual count since measles was declared eliminated in 2000 — including a child death in rural West Texas in February 2025, the first such death in a decade, as Kennedy's HHS issued a statement saying the decision to vaccinate is a personal one.

title: Trump Designates Antifa Domestic Terrorist Organization, Deploys FBI and IRS Against Democratic Donors
synopsis: On September 22, 2025, Trump signed an executive order designating Antifa — a decentralized, leaderless anti-fascist movement with no membership list, dues structure, or central command — as a domestic terrorist organization, directing all federal agencies to investigate, disrupt, and dismantle it; legal scholars noted the designation made no legal sense since the statutory framework for terrorist designations requires foreign organizations. The order was signed in the wake of the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, which Trump and his allies immediately blamed on a broader coordinated left-wing movement — despite investigators finding no evidence of any Antifa affiliation by the suspect. Two days later, Trump announced a second executive order targeting the financial networks of Radical Left Terrorists, explicitly naming Democratic billionaire donors George Soros and Reid Hoffman without citing any evidence of criminal activity. Reuters reported on October 9, 2025 that Stephen Miller was personally coordinating a multi-agency operation deploying the FBI, DHS, DOJ, IRS, and Treasury against liberal nonprofits. Trump's Truth Social post stated: The continuing violence from Radical Left Terrorists, in the aftermath of Charlie Kirk's assassination, must be stopped — though the IRS and Treasury Department's involvement in politically targeting opposition donors drew immediate comparisons to Nixon-era abuses of federal power. Congress passed no law authorizing the designations, and civil liberties organizations filed immediate legal challenges arguing Trump was essentially criminalizing political opposition under the guise of domestic terrorism enforcement.

title: Trump's Ukraine $350 Billion Hoax — Doubling the Real Aid Figure to Paint NATO as America's Con Artist
synopsis: From February 2025 onward, President Trump repeatedly and falsely claimed the United States had spent $350 billion supporting Ukraine's war against Russia, using the inflated figure to demand Ukraine repay the debt through a mineral extraction deal he pegged at $1 trillion and to portray NATO allies as freeloaders draining American taxpayers. The actual U.S. figure, according to Trump's own government, was approximately $183 billion in total appropriations — with only $83 billion actually disbursed as of December 2024 — and the Kiel Institute for the World Economy calculated the U.S. total at $119 billion; European nations had collectively provided approximately $138 billion, meaning Europe outspent the U.S. contrary to Trump's claims. Trump made the false $350 billion claim during his meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on February 28, 2025 — telling him we gave you $350 billion for military equipment — and repeated it in a March 4, 2025 address to Congress; Trump's own State Department issued a statement the same day that contradicted the figure. Trump also falsely claimed Ukraine started the war with Russia by refusing to make a deal — Russia launched its full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022 — and called Zelenskyy a dictator without elections, misleadingly ignoring that Ukrainian law requires suspension of elections during martial law. These false claims provided the rhetorical scaffolding for Trump's decision to freeze military aid to Ukraine and leverage the conflict as a conspiracy against American interests.

title: Trump's All-Out War on the Press: $32M in Forced Settlements, 215 Attack Posts, and a Media Offenders Blacklist
synopsis: Trump's second term saw his long-running enemy of the people rhetoric against journalism convert into systematic, government-backed suppression of the free press at a scale unprecedented in American history. The Freedom of the Press Foundation documented 215 anti-media posts by Trump on Truth Social in 2025, and Poynter's Press Freedom Watch recorded 76 distinct federal actions against journalists during the year. Media companies were coerced into paying $32 million in settlements: ABC paid $15 million toward Trump's presidential library to drop a defamation suit over George Stephanopoulos's on-air statement that Trump was found liable for sexual abuse, and Paramount paid $16 million to settle Trump's lawsuit over 60 Minutes editing — with critics noting Paramount was simultaneously seeking government approval for a Skydance merger, creating an explicit coercion dynamic. On November 28, 2025, the White House launched a media bias tracker on its official website naming and shaming outlets as misleading, biased, exposed, listing the Boston Globe, CBS News, and the Independent as media offenders of the week. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr opened eight investigations into NPR, PBS, ABC, NBC, and CBS; Congress voted in July 2025 to cancel $1.1 billion in subsidies for NPR and PBS. Independent journalist Mario Guevara, who had a valid U.S. work permit, was arrested while covering immigration protests in Atlanta, held for 110 days in conditions he described as including 22-hour daily solitary confinement, then deported to El Salvador — a country he had fled due to death threats — despite his charges being dropped.

title: Trump's Epstein Conspiracy Boomerang: Stoked Theories About Clinton and Obama, Got Burned by His Own Files
synopsis: For years, Trump and his MAGA base promoted conspiracy theories alleging that Jeffrey Epstein's victims included a client list implicating Democratic leaders — particularly Bill Clinton and Barack Obama — and that deep-state operatives had murdered Epstein in his jail cell to protect them. In July 2025, the Trump administration's own Justice Department and FBI abruptly reversed course on their pledge to release comprehensive Epstein records, announcing instead there was no secret client list of elites — triggering a furious backlash from Trump's own supporters, who accused Pam Bondi of covering up the files. The crisis intensified when the Wall Street Journal reported in July 2025 that Trump had written a birthday note with bawdy doodling to Epstein in 2003 — Trump filed a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the Journal, its parent company, and Rupert Murdoch, calling it fake news while simultaneously posting an AI-generated deepfake video of FBI agents arresting Barack Obama. On November 14, 2025, at Trump's urging, Attorney General Bondi ordered Manhattan U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton to investigate Epstein's ties to Clinton and other political foes — though none had been accused of sexual crimes — in what legal experts described as a weaponization of the DOJ for political conspiracy theory enforcement; the House Oversight Committee simultaneously subpoenaed depositions with Bill and Hillary Clinton. Trump's own long-documented personal friendship with Epstein — including descriptions of the two as close social companions throughout the 1990s and 2000s — meant the conspiracy playbook he deployed against rivals instead focused public attention squarely on himself.

title: They're Eating the Dogs: Springfield Ohio Haitian Pet-Eating Hoax Drives 2025 Immigration Crackdown
synopsis: The Haitians are eating pets disinformation campaign — launched from a fourth-hand Facebook post in a local Springfield, Ohio crime group — was amplified into national policy by Trump and JD Vance, with consequences that continued to shape immigration enforcement throughout 2025. Vance posted the baseless claim on September 9, 2024 to 11.1 million views on X, and Trump repeated it on the debate stage on September 11, 2024 — They're eating the dogs. They're eating the cats. They're eating the pets of the people that live there — despite debate moderators immediately citing Springfield's own city manager confirming no credible reports existed. Springfield Mayor Rob Rue and police repeatedly confirmed there were no credible reports or specific claims of pets being harmed, injured or abused by individuals within the immigrant community, and the one animal-cruelty case cited had occurred 160 miles away in Canton and involved a non-Haitian Ohio resident. The campaign continued to drive policy in 2025: the Trump administration cut Haitian Temporary Protected Status short by six months, setting expiration for August 3, 2025 rather than the original December deadline, stripping legal protection from thousands of Haitians who had arrived through lawful humanitarian parole programs. PolitiFact documented that Vance had cherry-picked limited statistics to claim an 81% murder spike linked to Springfield's Haitian community — a figure that masked a longer-term crime decline — and White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt continued to characterize all humanitarian parolees as illegal immigrants, despite federal judges ruling the characterization legally false.

title: King Trump's AI Propaganda Machine: 62 Deepfakes, a Fighter Jet Dropping Feces on Protesters, and False Crowd Photos
synopsis: A New York Times review published October 21, 2025 found that Trump had posted AI-generated images or videos at least 62 times to his Truth Social account since late 2022, with approximately half of the AI posts occurring in August and September 2025 alone — a pattern NBC News confirmed independently, identifying dozens of synthetic media posts going to Trump's 10.8 million Truth Social followers and 109.5 million X followers, with individual posts generating tens of millions of views. On October 18, 2025 — the day of nationwide No Kings rallies that organizers said drew nearly 7 million participants — Trump posted an AI video depicting himself wearing a crown in a fighter jet labeled King Trump, dropping what appeared to be feces on protesters in Times Square; guitarist Kenny Loggins issued a statement demanding his Danger Zone recording be removed immediately. The AI propaganda included a deepfake of Rep. Nancy Pelosi using a falsified voice to admit a crime, a July 20, 2025 video falsely showing FBI agents arresting Barack Obama posted at the height of the Epstein file controversy, an image of Trump dressed as pope posted on the White House's official X account in May 2025, and a deepfake promoting medbeds — a fictional cure-all popular in QAnon communities — that was eventually removed. Federal agencies posted AI-generated memes mocking detained migrants, and the White House communications operation embraced synthetic media as official government messaging strategy; Trump shrugged when asked about the pope image, saying I have nothing to do with it before pivoting to praise artificial intelligence as a priority of his administration.

title: Trump Bans AP from Oval Office and Air Force One, Then Seizes Control of the Entire Press Pool
synopsis: On February 14, 2025, the White House barred all Associated Press journalists from the Oval Office and Air Force One — citing the AP's refusal to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America in its stylebook — representing the first time a president had punished a wire service for non-compliance with a naming executive order. White House deputy chief of staff Taylor Budowich announced the ban in writing, stating that AP's commitment to misinformation forfeited its pool privileges. On February 25, 2025, press secretary Karoline Leavitt compounded the assault by announcing that the White House itself — not the independent White House Correspondents' Association — would henceforth determine which outlets participate in the presidential press pool, breaking more than 70 years of tradition. U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden ruled in April 2025 that the White House had likely violated the AP's First Amendment rights, but the administration defied his order, barring AP reporters from an April 14 Oval Office event despite the court's directive. The WHCA called the ban outrageous and a deep violation of press freedoms enshrined in our Constitution, while AP executive editor Julie Pace called it a plain violation of the First Amendment harming the 4 billion people who rely on AP daily.

title: FCC Chair Brendan Carr Weaponizes Broadcast License Reviews Against ABC, NBC, CBS for Critical Coverage
synopsis: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr — appointed by Trump in January 2025 and the author of the FCC chapter in Project 2025 — launched formal investigations into every major broadcast network except Fox News, including NBC, ABC, CBS, PBS, and NPR, throughout 2025 and 2026, citing alleged violations of the public interest standard in their broadcast licenses. In August 2025, Trump publicly called on the FCC to revoke ABC and NBC licenses on Truth Social, writing they should HAVE THEIR LICENSES REVOKED BY THE FCC for 97% negative coverage. On September 19, 2025, after ABC suspended Jimmy Kimmel's show under regulatory pressure, Trump said the FCC should act, while Carr told Fox News the Kimmel suspension was not the last shoe to drop. In April 2026, Carr ordered an early license review of Disney's eight ABC local stations — extraordinarily rare, as the FCC had not revoked a broadcast license in over four decades. FCC Democrat Anna Gomez wrote to Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro in May 2026 that what ABC faced was not a series of coincidental regulatory actions but a sustained, coordinated campaign of censorship and control, carried out through the weaponization of the FCC's authority.

title: Trump Extracts $31 Million in Settlements from ABC and CBS Through Litigation Pressure, Sues Des Moines Register
synopsis: Trump filed a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against CBS in October 2024, alleging that 60 Minutes deceptively edited an interview with Kamala Harris; Paramount/CBS settled for $16 million in July 2025, allocating the funds to Trump's presidential library, in a capitulation legal experts called a chilling precedent. ABC settled a separate Trump defamation suit in December 2024 for $15 million plus $1 million in legal fees — stemming from anchor George Stephanopoulos's statement that Trump had been found liable for rape — with ABC issuing a statement of regret it had not sought. In December 2024, Trump also filed suit against the Des Moines Register and pollster J. Ann Selzer in Polk County, Iowa, claiming their November 2 pre-election poll showing Harris leading by 3 points constituted brazen election interference under the Iowa Consumer Fraud Act; Gannett called the suit meritless. FCC Chair Carr openly cheered the CBS and ABC settlements, and the settlements were accompanied by editorial capitulations: CBS announced the cancellation of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert and agreed to install a Trump-friendly ombudsman to review CBS News coverage as a condition of FCC approval for Paramount's sale to Skydance. Legal experts widely warned the pattern of suits and settlements would generate a severe chilling effect on political journalism.

title: DOJ Subpoenas New York Times Reporters and Their Family Members to Unmask Sources
synopsis: In July 2026, the Trump Justice Department issued grand jury subpoenas to at least three New York Times journalists who had reported on security concerns with Trump's Qatar-gifted Air Force One jet, seeking to compel them to testify about their confidential sources — and then issued additional subpoenas to third-party phone carriers for the reporters' phone and text records, extending to spouses of two reporters and the mother of a third, a step legal experts called extraordinarily aggressive and unorthodox. The subpoenas were signed by Jay Clayton, Trump's U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, and covered call records dating to January 1, 2026 — months before the articles in question were published, suggesting broad fishing for source relationships. The Times moved to quash the subpoenas before U.S. District Judge Arun Subramanian, whose courtroom saw DOJ lawyers acknowledge they had served subpoenas before completing required preliminary investigative steps — an error prosecutors admitted was a consequence of trying to move too quickly. Judge Subramanian criticized the government's sloppy legal work and the DOJ withdrew the subpoenas on July 23, 2026, but then issued a defiant statement vowing the leak investigation remained ongoing. Attorney General Pam Bondi had earlier in 2025 revoked DOJ policies protecting journalists from subpoenas — policies established after abuses under prior administrations — explicitly to enable aggressive pursuit of government leakers.

title: Trump Permanently Expels AP from Air Force One and Presidential Pool Over Gulf of America Defiance
synopsis: On February 14, 2025, the White House formally barred Associated Press reporters and photographers from Air Force One and the Oval Office pool, an unprecedented punitive expulsion of the world's largest news wire service — which reaches an estimated 4 billion readers daily in 100 countries — solely because AP declined to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America in its global stylebook. Trump said publicly at Mar-a-Lago on February 18, We're going to keep them out until such time as they agree that it's the Gulf of America, framing a stylistic editorial decision as grounds for permanent exclusion from presidential coverage. AP photographers were physically blocked from the West Palm Beach airport tarmac to document Air Force One's arrival, and AP reporters were turned away from an Oval Office news conference with El Salvador President Nayib Bukele on April 14, 2025, in defiance of a court order by Judge Trevor McFadden issued just days earlier. The AP filed suit arguing First Amendment retaliation, and McFadden found the administration had likely violated free speech protections, but the White House appealed and continued its exclusions while the case moved through the courts. The White House simultaneously stripped the independent White House Correspondents' Association of its traditional role in selecting pool members, replacing it with administration-controlled access that Reuters, AP, and Bloomberg called a direct threat to the dissemination of reliable information about the presidency.

title: Trump's Fake News Rhetoric Graduates to Real Regulatory Action: FCC Opens Investigations of Every Major Network
synopsis: What began in Trump's first term as rhetorical attacks on fake news and the enemy of the people escalated in his second term into concrete federal regulatory action, with FCC Chairman Brendan Carr launching formal license investigations against NBC, ABC, CBS, NPR, and PBS while publicly coordinating messaging with the White House about potential license revocations. Carr told Reuters in March 2026 that all of that stuff is on the table when asked whether he would seek to revoke broadcast licenses, and used pending merger approvals as leverage to extract editorial concessions from networks, including CBS News's agreement to install an ombudsman and cancel The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. The only major network not under FCC investigation was Fox News, owned by Trump political ally Rupert Murdoch — a selective enforcement pattern that FCC Democrat Anna Gomez called a sustained, coordinated campaign of censorship and control in May 2026. Carr wrote op-eds in Breitbart and appeared on Fox News repeatedly to frame license threats as protecting the public interest, while press freedom organizations noted the FCC had not revoked a major broadcast license in over 40 years. The CPJ's first-100-days report in April 2025 found Trump's regulatory actions had created a chilling effect unprecedented in modern American history, with the administration's threats no longer vague but directed against specific media outlets in their entirety.

title: Trump Signs Executive Order Defunding NPR and PBS, Congress Rescinds $1.1 Billion from CPB
synopsis: On May 1, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14290, Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Biased Media, directing the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and all federal agencies to immediately cease Federal funding for NPR and PBS, calling neither entity capable of presenting a fair, accurate, or unbiased portrayal of current events. The order — which PBS CEO Paula Kerger called blatantly unlawful when it was issued in the middle of the night — instructed the CPB board to revise its grant criteria by June 30, 2025 to prohibit any indirect funding flowing to NPR or PBS, and ordered HHS to investigate whether both entities complied with employment non-discrimination laws as a backdoor enforcement mechanism. CPB sued the administration over Trump's simultaneous attempt to fire three of its five board members via email, and the CPB's president stated flatly that the organization is not a federal executive agency subject to the President's authority. Despite those legal challenges, a Republican-controlled Congress subsequently rescinded $1.1 billion in already-appropriated CPB funding — supporting approximately 1,000 public radio stations and 350 public TV stations — and the CPB announced in August 2025 that it would begin shutdown proceedings. NPR CEO Katherine Maher called the order an affront to the First Amendment and said the less than 0.0001% of the federal budget at stake made clear the attack was political, not fiscal.

title: ICE Arrests Journalists Covering Immigration — Spanish-Language Reporter Estefany Rodriguez Detained 16 Days
synopsis: On March 4, 2026, ICE agents surrounded the marked Nashville Noticias press vehicle carrying Estefany Rodriguez Florez — a Colombian-born journalist who had fled death threats for her crime coverage in Bogota — and detained her without presenting a judicial warrant, in what her attorneys called a retaliatory arrest targeting a reporter frequently critical of ICE. Rodriguez was held in ICE custody for over 16 days, transferred to Etowah County Jail in Alabama and then to the South Louisiana ICE Processing Center in Basile, Louisiana, before a judge finally allowed bond; she was released March 20, 2026. The Committee to Protect Journalists documented at least two similar cases: journalist Mario Guevara was detained near Atlanta and ultimately deported, having fled El Salvador after receiving death threats. The CPJ also documented the October 2025 arrest of British political commentator Sami Hamdi at San Francisco International Airport after his visa was revoked without notification, and in January 2026, FBI agents raided the Virginia home of Washington Post reporter Hannah Natanson and seized her electronic devices and work laptop in a leak investigation. Press freedom groups noted that ICE also arrested independent journalist Georgia Fort in January 2026 while she was covering a Minnesota church protest against immigration enforcement, with journalists Don Lemon, Junn Bollmann, and Michael Walker Beute facing similar federal charges from the same event.

title: Hegseth Forces Pentagon Press Corps Exodus: 30+ Outlets Surrender Credentials Rather Than Sign Censorship Pledge
synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth — a former Fox News host — issued a 17-page Pentagon press access directive in September 2025 requiring credentialed journalists to sign a pledge agreeing not to report information not approved for public release by an appropriate authorizing official, explicitly including unclassified information, under threat of credential revocation and loss of access. At least 30 major news organizations — including Reuters, AP, The New York Times, The Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, CNN, Fox News, NBC, ABC, CBS, NPR, Axios, Politico, The Guardian, The Atlantic, Bloomberg, and dozens of military-focused publications — refused to sign the policy. On October 15, 2025, the deadline day, dozens of journalists carried boxes of files, chairs, a copying machine, and personal items out of the Pentagon building in a historic departure, with roughly 40-50 reporters vacating their long-established press workspaces. The Pentagon Press Association called the new rules a direct attack on the freedom of the press. Hegseth had earlier in May 2025 required journalists to have official escorts throughout most of the Pentagon building, and had launched an aggressive internal leak investigation that resulted in the removal of senior military officials. Only One America News agreed to the new access terms.

title: CPJ Reports Unprecedented U.S. Journalist Safety Crisis: 530 Reporters Trained in 4 Months vs. 20 in All of 2022
synopsis: The Committee to Protect Journalists reported in its April 2025 first-100-days assessment that requests for safety training, threat counseling, and emergency assistance from U.S.-based journalists had surged to historic levels — with CPJ providing safety training to more than 530 journalists in the United States between November 8, 2024 and March 7, 2025, compared to just 20 reporters trained throughout all of 2022. Journalists sought guidance on field safety, digital security, protecting confidential sources from DOJ subpoenas, potential IRS audits as political retaliation, immigration risks for non-citizen reporters crossing U.S. borders, and defense against doxxing and online harassment campaigns. CPJ safety specialist Colin Pereira noted that the speed of the deterioration surprised even veteran observers: Newsrooms now need to have support structures to assist and help journalists manage threats long-term — and they need to do it quickly. The CPJ noted a qualitative shift from Trump's first term: administration attacks were no longer vague enemy of the people rhetoric but direct, named targeting of specific outlets — AP, NPR, PBS, CBS, NBC, ABC — in their entirety. On World Press Freedom Day 2026, CPJ and Amnesty International USA jointly warned of relentless targeting of journalists, citing the arrest of Georgia Fort while covering an immigration protest, a pattern reminiscent of repressive government tactics CPJ has documented around the world. The U.S. fell dramatically in the Reporters Without Borders 2025 Press Freedom Index.
